newsitem.title: UK: Clarke - UK outside EMU means less negotiating scope.
newsitem.headline: Clarke - UK outside EMU means less negotiating scope.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday Britain's negotiating position within the European Union could be seriously reduced if it did not sign up for the first wave of European Economic and Monetary Union, set for 1999.

Asked if Britain could opt out of the first wave and remain at the negotiating table, Clarke said: "You could remain at the negotiating table but your ability to have influence at that table might be seriously reduced."
"But logically it shouldn't," Clarke told the Treasury Select Committee in parliament. "The countries that stay out will have an interest on the way in which EMU goes ahead."
